papers.title: PrivFusion: Privacy-Preserving Model Fusion via Decentralized Federated Graph Matching
papers.venue_full_name: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
papers.research_problem: Fuse independently trained models while limiting disclosure of model activations and weights to other model owners.
papers.key_idea: PrivFusion combines locally perturbed graph representations, decentralized neuron matching, and a perturbation-filter adapter. Mechanistic reading is from the differently titled 2023 author preprint, not the 2024 version of record.
papers.technical_mechanism: Author preprint arXiv:2311.03396v1, Sections III–IV: represent neurons/channels as nodes and weights as edges; perturb activation features with Laplace noise and bounded weight features with a multi-bit mechanism; combine activation/weight affinities for graph matching; align neurons, apply Gaussian perturbation and smoothing, and average aligned weights.
papers.assumptions: Author preprint: honest-but-curious model owners; agreed tasks and compatible public architectures; aligned input/output neurons; a few inference examples to obtain activation features; bounded weight features and calibrated sensitivities/privacy budgets. The fusion stage avoids retraining but is not strictly data-free.
papers.main_contribution: A decentralized privacy-aware graph-matching fusion procedure, with author-stated local-DP mechanisms and privacy–utility experiments on image tasks and a two-party healthcare construction.
papers.limitations: Content reviewed in arXiv:2311.03396v1 only; the final TKDE text was not accessed. Small-network evaluations and graph-matching memory cost limit scalability evidence. The healthcare data originate from 17 hospitals but the reported experiment groups 15 regions into two parties; this is not evidence of a live 17-hospital federation. Strong regional heterogeneity can degrade fusion substantially (preprint Table IV). Privacy unit, sensitivity calibration, approximate-DP delta, and composition across releases require explicit accounting before asserting end-to-end patient-level privacy.

papers.research_problem: One-shot federation needs to combine heterogeneous client models without a shared auxiliary dataset or repeated client communication.
papers.key_idea: Generate synthetic inputs from uploaded models, then distill their averaged logits into a server student.
papers.technical_mechanism: Train a server generator using ensemble classification, batch-normalization statistics and a teacher-student boundary-disagreement objective; alternate generation and KL-based ensemble-to-student distillation after the client models are uploaded once.
papers.assumptions: Server access to client models and their BN statistics for the stated generation loss, compatible input/output-label semantics and server-side generation/distillation compute; raw auxiliary examples are not required at the server.
papers.main_contribution: Supplies a one-shot behavioral-fusion route across differing architectures and a contrast to coordinate averaging or curvature-weighted fusion.
papers.limitations: Data-free refers to the absence of raw auxiliary training data at the server, not absence of local training data, BN statistics or server optimization. Visual dissimilarity of generated images does not establish privacy: the paper leaves additional privacy mechanisms and attack analysis for future work. Model access and synthesis quality remain substantive assumptions.
